en: Salutation to the one whose nature is the reality of the syllable Oṃ, whose essence is divine knowledge; salutation to the one of great splendor beyond the ether, possessing the vigor of Indra’s power. || 1 ||
To him whose path is accessible to those who have destroyed their envy, whose self-conduct consists of approaching the unapproachable,
who effects liberation from impurity, and whose glory is bestowed by the seed-syllable *ṛhīṃ*.
To him who is the end of delusions such as ignorance, who assumes many bodies, who is the field for the great prosperity of his devotees, and who is the supreme reciter of the seed-syllable *klīṃ*.
We bow to the one who destroys existence, whose lips are red as a king’s blood,
whose testicles tremble with his gait, and whose arms are beautifully struck down.

Salutations to him who has abandoned pride and attachment, whose mind is restrained by Yama and other deities, who has attained mastery over all things, who is shaven-headed, and who is free from malice.

Salutations to you, whose various forms are untouched by the net of speech, even that which is most worthy of praise; to you, who are pleased by the wealth of asceticism, and whose fame is extolled by the Lord of the Gods.
To her who dwells within the inner chamber of the jewel of light, who resides in the internal abode, and whose sovereign power is sung in the Vedas; (7)
Salutation to the one who is the cause of the destruction of the states associated with the fear of wind and the other [humors], who is the cause of the cause,
who has become the very self of the world, and who is the slayer of the six enemies.
To the one who rescued the host of gods, to the destroyer of the abode of the asuras;
to the two eyes, to the seer, to the eye, to the great-souled one who is consciousness and awareness.
To the God of the gods of gods, the protector of the earth and the gods,
the foremost among those who perform sacrifices, who is gratified by the recitation of the seed-syllable *drāṃ*.

Salutations to the consciousness known as Dattātreya, who is a forest fire to the woods of latent impressions (vāsanā), whose body is smeared with dust, and who is the refuge for ascetics and renunciants.
Salutations to the one who is the source of sacrifice, who is born from the mouth, who goes to the abode of the stars,
whose form is untouched by great speed, who has assumed a manifest form, and who is of diverse forms.
Salutation to the one who bestows wisdom upon men, to the illustrious Yaśasvin,
to the captivating one with radiant limbs, and to Sambhu, the son of Atri.
Salutation to the one who has liberated the hosts of immortals, to the wise one whose body is steadfast,
to the one who can deceive even the most powerful, and to the one who delights in sacrifice and oblation.

To him whose majesty is sung by the gods, who cuts through the power of the enemy of the gods (Śiva), who is the object of worship for the shaven-headed (the Buddha), who is a self-restrained ascetic, and who wears a golden garland; 15.
And for those whose afflictions and diseases have departed, and who possess a splendor bestowed by gold,
they undertake the conduct of the lords of ascetics as a medicine for their human condition.
Salutations to the one worshipped by the most excellent yogis, who extends the thread [of creation];
salutations to the one whose sacred bathing place is the song of his own self, who is the glory of Ma, and who possesses six hands.
To him whose supreme head is composed of splendor, who performs the acts of impelling and being impelled,
who is the knower of loss, gain, and death, and who is the object of true devotion through the utterance of *Oṃ*— to him [I bow].
Salutations to the one who removes the weariness of body, speech, and mind; to the one whose nature transcends the range of vision;
to the one clad in garments of deer-skin; to the illuminator of the true reality of man.
Salutations to the one who has conquered his own enemies by causing their sins to flee and bowing down; who dwells in his own abode;
who is of a single form throughout the three worlds; who is established in immortality; and who is the kinsman of the breath of life.

Homage to the one who transcends the impulse of the senses and whose power arises from his conduct; to the one who is free from pride and anger, and who brings about the perfect accomplishment of his disciples.
To Gaṅgā, who was deprived of her feet; to the one whose self was impelled by the urging of the goad;
to the younger brother; to the one who [drank] the water of Alarka’s suffering; and to the one of unbroken self.

To the one whose seed-syllable is *hīṃ*, who is Arjuna and Jyeṣṭha, whose self is revealed through vision, whose mind is satisfied by prostration, and who is an ascetic and a celibate student. || 23 ||
Thus ends this true hymn of praise, which bestows happiness upon the Creator;
it is the Lord of Ascetics, woven through the Manus, and the giver of the state of the Supreme Brahman.
